item.title: Platform Review Checklist
item.description:
How to use it#

Use this checklist to review your own design before building, or a team’s design at an architecture board or production-readiness review. Score each area 0–3 and record evidence.

1. Goals and SLOs#

  • Business goals and users defined? SLOs, RTO and RPO per service tier?
  • Red flags: “five nines” for everything; no owner per service.

2. Cluster topology#

  • Managed or self-managed — and why? How many clusters, by environment/region/tenancy? Zones?
  • Upgrade cadence and process? Clusters reproducible from code?
  • Red flags: hand-built snowflake clusters; versions more than two minors behind; single-zone production.

3. Workloads#

  • Requests/limits, probes, PDBs, topology spread, autoscaling for every production workload?
  • Stateful services on managed databases or mature operators? Backups tested?
  • Red flags: BestEffort Pods in prod; liveness probes that check dependencies; databases without tested restore.

4. Networking#

  • Gateway API (not ingress-nginx); TLS everywhere; DNS automation?
  • Default-deny NetworkPolicies; egress control; IP plan for growth?
  • Service mesh justified?
  • Red flags: one LoadBalancer per app; flat network; retired ingress controller.

5. Security#

  • OIDC for humans; least-privilege RBAC; no cluster-admin for CI or apps?
  • Pod Security restricted; policy as code enforced; secrets in an external store; workload identity?
  • Signed images verified at admission; SBOMs; runtime detection; audit logs?
  • Red flags: secrets in Git; :latest images; privileged Pods; shared admin kubeconfigs.

6. Delivery#

  • Build once, promote by digest; DevSecOps scans; GitOps pull model?
  • Progressive delivery with automated analysis and rollback? Database migration strategy?
  • Change management automated with evidence; release orchestration where needed?
  • Red flags: CI with production credentials; manual helm upgrade in prod; per-environment rebuilds.

7. Platform and developer experience#

  • Golden paths for common tasks; catalog with owners; self-service infrastructure APIs?
  • Platform run as a product with users, roadmap, metrics and SLOs?
  • Red flags: ticket-driven provisioning; portal without automation; mandated tools nobody likes.

8. Observability and resilience#

  • OpenTelemetry instrumentation; metrics, logs, traces correlated; SLO burn-rate alerts; runbooks?
  • Timeouts, retries (one layer), circuit breakers; DR strategy per tier; drills; chaos experiments?
  • Red flags: alerts on CPU only; no tracing; untested DR.

9. Cost and operations#

  • Cost allocation by team (labels enforced); showback; budgets and anomaly alerts?
  • Rightsizing, autoscaling, spot, commitments, non-prod schedules?
  • On-call, incident process, postmortems, platform team capacity?
  • Red flags: no cost visibility; requests far above usage; heroic on-call.

Scoring rubric#

Score Meaning
0 Missing
1 Mentioned, not designed
2 Designed with some gaps
3 Designed and evidenced (tests, numbers, prototypes, drills)

Ready for production when no area is 0, security and resilience score 3 for Tier 0/1 services, and all gaps have owners and dates.

item.title: Cloud Native Quick Reference
item.description:
Kubernetes objects at a glance#

Need Object
Stateless app Deployment (+ HPA, PDB)
Stateful app StatefulSet + PVC (or operator / managed service)
Per-node agent DaemonSet
Batch / scheduled Job / CronJob
Stable address Service
North-south traffic Gateway + HTTPRoute
Config / secrets ConfigMap / Secret (+ External Secrets)
Isolation & budgets Namespace, ResourceQuota, LimitRange, NetworkPolicy
Availability during drains PodDisruptionBudget
New API types CRD + operator

kubectl essentials#

kubectl get pods -n shop -o wide            # what is running where
kubectl describe pod <pod> -n shop          # events and reasons
kubectl logs deploy/orders -n shop -f       # logs
kubectl events -n shop --types=Warning      # recent problems
kubectl diff -f k8s/                        # preview changes
kubectl rollout status deploy/orders        # watch a rollout
kubectl rollout undo deploy/orders          # roll back
kubectl debug -it <pod> --image=busybox     # ephemeral debug container
kubectl auth can-i delete pods --as=jane    # check RBAC
kubectl top pods -n shop                    # resource usage

Secure defaults#

Area Default
Pod security Namespace label pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
Container non-root, read-only root FS, drop ALL capabilities, seccomp RuntimeDefault
Network Default-deny NetworkPolicy + explicit allows (incl. DNS)
Images Minimal base, scanned, signed, SBOM, deployed by digest
Secrets External store + External Secrets Operator; etcd encryption at rest
Access OIDC humans, least-privilege RBAC, read-only prod, workload identity for Pods

Delivery#

Topic Rule of thumb
Artifacts Build once, sign, promote by digest
Packaging Helm for packages, Kustomize for overlays
Deployment GitOps pull (Argo CD / Flux); folders per environment, not branches
Rollout Canary with automated analysis (Argo Rollouts / Flagger)
Secrets in Git Never plaintext: External Secrets, Sealed Secrets or SOPS
Governance Risk-based automated approvals; orchestration for multi-team releases
DORA Deploy frequency, lead time, change failure rate, recovery time

Platform engineering#

Concept One-liner
Platform as a product Developers are customers; adoption is earned
Golden path Opinionated supported route with guardrails
IDP planes Developer control, integration & delivery, resources, observability, security
Portal Backstage: catalog, templates, TechDocs, plugins
Infra APIs Crossplane / kro claims and compositions
DevEx Feedback loops, cognitive load, flow state
Maturity aspects Investment, adoption, interfaces, operations, measurement

SLO maths#

SLO Downtime / 30 days Error budget
99% 7.2 h 1%
99.5% 3.6 h 0.5%
99.9% 43 min 0.1%
99.95% 22 min 0.05%
99.99% 4.3 min 0.01%

Fast-burn page (99.9% SLO): burn rate ≥ 14.4 over 1 h and 5 min = 2% of monthly budget in one hour.
